'Terminates or eventually repeats' is the class RepeatingDecimal; the definitions of rational and irrational are firm. q3 (continued fraction) goes through the RELATIONS.md chain instance_of ∘ subclass_of ⊑ instance_of: rational ⊑ finite and irrational ⊑ infinite continued fraction, the two firm and disjoint (2026-10-31; the old q3 conjunction moved to the propositional query type).

bridge_refs.rat_repeat: Every rational number has a decimal expansion that terminates or eventually repeats.
bridge_refs.rat_cf: Every rational number has a finite continued fraction expansion.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): a fraction p/q whose square is 2
fol (arithmetic): the ratio of a square's diagonal to its side

fol.notes: Being rational (a fraction p/q) is the model's belief: uninterpreted predicates, since built-in reals cannot make √2 rational. q1 asks about a fraction whose square is 2; the only numbers whose square is 2 are ±√2, and the question is read as being about √2 (sqrt_sq). q2's ratio is diag_ratio, equal to √2 by the stored fact about squares.

rat_frac.says: Every rational number can be written as a fraction p/q of two whole numbers (and every such fraction is rational).

irr_def.says: An irrational number is a number that is not rational.

sqrt_sq.says: The square of the square root of 2 is 2.

diag.says: The diagonal of a square is the square root of 2 times its side, so diagonal : side = √2.
